statusMessage: At 23:14 the investigators are working separately. Linnea is at Rask House with Anneli Rask, where the recovered withdrawal record links Nils's money to Emil, Freja, and Oskar. Erik has arrived at the North Channel Ferry Terminal; the floodlit service lanes are nearly deserted, but Nils Rask, Jesper Holm, and Ida Brandt remain inside the operations and workshop buildings.

signal_house.name: Constable Solveig Brandt
signal_house.description: Vesperholm's composed local constable, rain darkening the shoulders of her uniform.

signal_house.name: Dr. Emil Jessen
signal_house.description: The island physician, silver-haired and quietly attentive beside the temporary mortuary table.

signal_house.name: Oskar Lind
signal_house.description: The Saint Vigga custodian, now under arrest and seated under Constable Brandt's guard after admitting that he staged Annika's body.

signal_house.name: Freja Moller
signal_house.description: The salvage diver, now under arrest and held separately from Oskar after denying involvement in Annika's death.

saint_vigga_fort.name: Erik Sund
saint_vigga_fort.description: A weather observer in a salt-stiff coat, more comfortable with instruments than speculation.

marine_laboratory.name: Leif Arden
marine_laboratory.description: The marine laboratory's sharp-featured deputy director, impatient beneath professional restraint.

marine_laboratory.name: Rune Falk
marine_laboratory.description: A retired tide engineer with heavy brows, oil-black nails, and no patience for automated systems.

glassworks_museum.name: Karin Ravn
glassworks_museum.description: Annika's elder sister and the museum's austere director, grief held behind a level stare.

glassworks_museum.name: Magnus Hald
glassworks_museum.description: A broad-handed master glassblower whose spectacles catch the furnace glow.

gull_house_hotel.name: Marta Eide
gull_house_hotel.description: Gull House's elegant proprietor, warm in manner and absolute about her guests' privacy.

gull_house_hotel.name: Kasper Birk
gull_house_hotel.description: A young island courier with a quick smile, wet hair, and the alertness of someone who hears everything.

ferry_terminal.name: Nils Rask
ferry_terminal.description: Director of North Channel Ferries, tailored and composed beneath the operations-room fluorescents.

ferry_terminal.name: Jesper Holm
ferry_terminal.description: A young ferry dispatcher with bitten nails and a headset resting around his neck.

ferry_terminal.name: Ida Brandt
ferry_terminal.description: A dryly observant deck mechanic in blue coveralls, Constable Brandt's younger sister.

saltline_clinic.name: Asta Berg
saltline_clinic.description: The clinic's blunt, watchful senior nurse and pharmacist.

saltline_clinic.name: Tove Jessen
saltline_clinic.description: A composed clinic administrator with a precise memory for schedules.

moller_salvage.name: Johan Lykke
moller_salvage.description: An elderly fisherman repairing nets with deliberate, tar-darkened fingers.

saint_oda_archive.name: Pastor Elias Nygaard
saint_oda_archive.description: Saint Oda's gentle archivist, carrying a ring of small brass drawer keys.

saint_oda_archive.name: Petra Dahl
saint_oda_archive.description: A regional investigative journalist with a damp notebook and an assessing gaze.

rask_house.name: Anneli Rask
rask_house.description: An architect and Nils Rask's estranged wife, cool-eyed and exact in her language.

items.name: Clock escapement key
items.description: A modified clock key whose stop marks can be compared with the Saint Vigga mechanism.

items.name: Dated telegraph strip
items.description: A narrow station printout carrying a sequence of harbor signals from the evening Annika died.

items.name: Orange sling fragment
items.description: A torn high-load sling fragment carrying black hull paint and Tidegate grit.

items.name: Structured withdrawal slip
items.description: A bank counterfoil grouping three cash withdrawals beneath misleading repair references.

evidence.title: The Saint Vigga Drowning
evidence.summary: Hydrographer Dr. Annika Ravn, 41, was found dead and wet beneath the storm bell inside Saint Vigga's dry locked chamber at 20:18.

evidence.title: Handwritten camera-isolation docket
evidence.summary: A handwritten Thursday docket orders terminal cameras two and four offline from 18:29 to 18:36 for a 'union inspection.' The access-alert register records both outages, but the surrounding operational records contain no corresponding formal work order.

inventoryItem.name: Handwritten camera-isolation docket
inventoryItem.description: A copied Thursday operational docket ordering terminal cameras two and four offline from 18:29 to 18:36 for a supposed union inspection. It carries Jesper Holm's acknowledgement but no work-order reference or supervisor authorization.

evidence.title: Seven-minute camera gap
evidence.summary: Jesper disabled terminal cameras two and four from 18:29 to 18:36 on Nils Rask's instruction.

evidence.title: Thursday ferry-company vehicle register
evidence.summary: A certified copy of North Channel Ferries' Thursday vehicle register, listing registrations, vehicle classes, assigned departments, and recorded status. It has not yet been compared with the service-lane sighting or workshop records.

inventoryItem.name: Thursday company ferry vehicle register
inventoryItem.description: A certified copy of North Channel Ferries' Thursday vehicle register, listing registrations, vehicle classes, assigned departments, and recorded status.

evidence.title: Annika's sealed note to Petra
evidence.summary: Annika tells Petra that the promised Eidolon evidence is real but that her account was incomplete. She warns that the brass cylinder was a decoy, points toward archive pages that do not belong and a ledger that conceals its nature, and insists Petra account for Annika's own part in 1995 before publishing.

inventoryItem.name: Note from Annika to Petra
inventoryItem.description: Annika's sealed deposit to Petra Dahl. The opened note says the promised Eidolon evidence is real but incomplete, warns that the brass cylinder was a decoy, and points toward replaced archive pages and a disguised ledger.

evidence.title: Modified key stopped the fort clock
evidence.summary: Under magnification, the paired stop marks on the modified escapement key exactly match fresh impressions inside Saint Vigga's clock mechanism. The clock was deliberately stopped with this key, contradicting Oskar Lind's explanation that age or storm damage halted it.

evidence.title: Oskar staged Saint Vigga
evidence.summary: Oskar admits operating the bell lift, stopping the clock, planting blue glass, and locking the chamber after Freja delivered Annika's body.

evidence.title: A skiff returned from Saint Vigga
evidence.summary: Johan saw and heard an older diesel service skiff returning from Saint Vigga around 19:47.

evidence.title: Nils funded three participants
evidence.summary: Structured withdrawals from Nils's accounts align with payments or debt relief for Emil, Freja, and Oskar before Annika's abduction.
